result.summary: Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-006.md covering all 5 REQ-006 acceptance criteria plus a supporting rendered-page check, modeled on docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-004.md's structure. Every script/curl command in the spec was actually executed against messages/kk.json, messages/ru.json, src/app/globals.css, and a real npm run build && npm run start server on localhost:3000 during authoring, with real observed output copied into the spec verbatim (server was stopped again afterward). AC1 (non-empty/translated values): node script found 177/177 keys non-empty and identified 34 identical ru/kk value pairs, each independently verified as a legitimate untranslatable literal (person names, country/role codes, date-tab codes, city-name proper nouns, brand/contact/license literals, one numeric value, one acronym) -- including re-deriving (not trusting) REVIEWER's step-10 judgment call that Footer.licenseCode='КОД'/licenseBrand='БРЕНД' are genuine established Kazakh loanwords by confirming both words appear natively elsewhere in the file's own prose (код in Streams.foundationBody matching ru.json's own usage; бренд in 6 other keys). AC2 (ogLocale): confirmed 'kk_KZ' both in the source JSON and in the rendered <meta property="og:locale"> tag on the built /kk page, with /ru as a control showing 'ru_RU' to prove the tag is genuinely locale-driven. AC3 (Cyrillic Kazakh throughout): confirmed 569 Kazakh-specific letter occurrences (Ә/Ғ/Қ/Ң/Ө/Ұ/Ү/Һ/І, both cases) spread across 12 of 18 letter-forms, and that every Latin-script match of length>=5 is either a JSON key name or an already-accounted-for proper noun/brand/acronym/role-title literal, not translatable prose. AC4 (status labels lowercase): confirmed all 8 status values lowercase in source, confirmed the unconditional .status{text-transform:uppercase} CSS rule at globals.css:152, and confirmed all 8 status spans render lowercase in the built page's HTML, byte-for-byte matching the source values. AC5 (no exclamation/slogan/emoji): grep -n "!" exited 1 with no output; a node Unicode-range emoji scan returned 0 matches; a full manual read of messages/kk.json's title/lede/cta* values found only plain declarative/imperative copy, no hype slogans. AC6 (supporting, rendered-page evidence): confirmed no MISSING_MESSAGE/IntlError markers on /kk or /ru, spot-checked 4 real Kazakh strings across 4 namespaces (Nav, Hero with t.rich() emphasis, Doors, Footer) rendering correctly with real Kazakh-specific letters, confirmed HTTP 200 and <html lang="kk">, and wrote the full 4-viewport/theme content-completeness procedure per qa_testing_guide.md §5. Also added a dedicated CFP-verbatim-domain-term check re-deriving that Event/Chapter/Talk/Speaker have zero remaining untranslated instances (the exact defect class REVIEWER's step-08 review caught and required two rework cycles to fix) and CFP appears exactly twice, matching the requirement text's claim that CFP is the sole genuine verbatim-English domain term.
